backbone: RSW-type crossing and localization estimates give tightness of interfaces; a discrete four-change boundary observable, via transfer-row algebra, solves a boundary problem identifying every subsequential limit's Loewner driver as SLE_kappa.
quote: The proof combines finite connection comparisons below one, localization in irregular tiled disks, and a boundary observable that determines the limiting Loewner driver.

backbone: Exact closed-circuit orthogonality identities are transported to open rim arcs via plugs and arm estimates; a discrete holomorphic observable's unique boundary problem identifies every subsequential crossing limit as Cardy's formula.
quote: The resulting boundary-value problem has the conformal map to an equilateral triangle as its unique solution. This common boundary problem identifies every subsequential crossing limit.

backbone: Bethe-ansatz finite-word formulas (Slavnov determinants) are pushed to thermodynamic row kernels, giving an angular transfer representation whose two leading current modes yield Gaussian correlations with variance 1/arcsin(c/2).
quote: The finite formulas of Section~\ref{sec:finite} reduce a row word to sums over finitely many selected Bethe roots. To pass to a plane kernel we must control those sums

backbone: Transfer-matrix particle-sector spectral penalties bound slab traversals and short segments, giving curve compactness; cited puncture-lamination convergence plus exclusion of invisible paths and backtracking identifies limit loops with CLE4.
quote: Our first geometric estimate bounds the number of times the double-dimer loops can cross a slab of fixed positive width. We prove it in a finite Temperleyan rectangle.

backbone: Burn-in density bounds, hidden-gradient decay and visible exact modes give contraction over one long block, iterated to logarithmic times for the upper bound; a slow observable gives the lower bound.
quote: The proof establishes fixed-time comparisons first, then makes a single sufficiently long block uniform before iterating it.

backbone: Build a stable radial potential (core with four-particle clusters plus successively added Kac long-range attractions) and show via convex free-energy analysis that supporting slopes persist, giving a common derivative jump.
quote: We construct a stable radial pair potential in three dimensions whose canonical free energy has a strict downward derivative jump at one common finite positive inverse temperature throughout an open interval of positive densities.

backbone: A degree-six polynomial constraint on posterior laws is preserved by channel steps and products; induction on depth with certified polynomial inequalities makes E[A] subadditive, forcing decay at dλ²≤1.
quote: We construct a degree-six polynomial $H$ for which the additional constraint $\E H(p)\geq0$ is preserved by both channel steps and the combination of observations.

backbone: Multipoint radius estimates give moments of a canonical Green-potential trace mass that fix the gauge; explicit batch covers give the upper bound and past-mass comparison the lower bound.
quote: For each \(0<\kappa<8\), we construct a deterministic Hausdorff gauge that almost surely assigns positive finite measure to every nontrivial compact positive-time segment

backbone: Construct an equivariant stochastic-localization sampler: Brownian observations of edges with posterior-mean drift from a free spanning-tree response field, inverted deterministically via a uniform response bound into a Borel rule.
quote: We prove the unrestricted graphwise statement by a different construction: the same Borel rule works for every graph in our class, independently of any random-graph law.

backbone: Spin/percolation cuts give circuit and moment bounds; reflection positivity with a spectral sum rule fixes the covariance, boundary comparison removes boundary effects, and Wick recursion identifies subsequential limits as GFF.
quote: The proof combines reflection positivity, a spectral sum rule, and boundary comparison with Gaussian moment identities.

backbone: Joint tightness from circuit and comparison estimates; reflection positivity plus screening identifies the height as GFF; recursive stopped two-valued local sets of that field then identify every subsequential cluster limit.
quote: Our proof first obtains joint tightness, then identifies every subsequential limit as the canonical construction of \cref{thm:main}.

backbone: Matching bounds: an upper comparison via Haar spectral-rotation identities and ultrametric overlap structure, and a cavity lower bound with a maximizing field, joined by concavity of the field functional.
quote: The lower bound will identify a field whose conditional two-spin products equal the overlap quantile.

backbone: Integrated forcing bounds give polynomial concentration of a capped last-satisfiable index; a Poisson interpolation comparison between system sizes plus a deterministic approximate-superadditivity lemma forces the normalized centers to converge.
quote: This paper gives an alternative proof, using concentration of a capped last satisfiable index and a comparison between different system sizes.

backbone: Spins are built from Brownian innovations via a stochastic-localization field equation; response-row bounds and an integrable Osgood comparison show observations sharing innovations coincide, giving an equivariant factor.
quote: The complete noise and drift calculation then gives an integrable Osgood-type inequality for $V$, forcing $V=0$.

backbone: Integrable dilute-loop transfer identities, polynomial vacua and vertex-operator angular calculations give exact marked-polygon masses; radial estimates convert them to polygon diameter/length tails, transferred to walks for the n^{3/4} diameter.
quote: We construct the two zero-loop-weight vectors needed here by interpolation and identify their physical normalization.

backbone: Conditional coin-flow contraction bounds averaged ordered marginals; an eight-block Fourier bound lifts them to all irreducibles, and the upper-bound lemma gives TV mixing; a support count gives the lower bound.
quote: The full permutation law after $1600d$ shuffles converges to uniform in total variation as $d\to\infty$, uniformly over the initial deck, while a support count gives a lower bound of $2d-O(1)$.

backbone: Schur complement reduces to symmetric bit matrices at corank one; expected admissible appended columns are bounded by a lattice-quotient potential whose moment along principal-minor paths is 2^{o(N)}.
quote: A reduction to corank one then turns singularity into a question about appending a new column to a nonsingular matrix \(B\).

backbone: Reduce to the qualitative form; from unboundedly many categoricity cardinals build EM presentations, reverse strong maps, then amalgamation, independence and one-dimensional geometry so models are determined by dimension.
quote: For each infinite bound on the L\"owenheim--Skolem number there is a uniform threshold such that categoricity in any one cardinal at or above that threshold implies categoricity

backbone: Represent the automorphism by a Borel map (Slaman–Woodin); four-value recovery computes t generically from F-values; Sacks category cone avoidance removes auxiliary reals giving π^{-1}(a)≤a and symmetrically π(a)≤a.
quote: Since recovery holds on a comeager set, Lemma~\ref{lem:avoidance} removes the auxiliary degrees and yields $\pi^{-1}(\mathbf a)\leT\mathbf a$ for every degree $\mathbf a$.

backbone: Construct unique-witness polynomial gadgets: a rank-one elliptic curve with height control gives a uniquely represented growth function, then a unique power graph, digit containment, and unique halting-run encoding.
quote: We first obtain unique arithmetic witnesses, then a unique encoding of the accepting run.

backbone: Construct CFI-type F3-linear grid structures with opposite answers; a central-extension group action, sparse supports and counting-equivalence homogeneity show any CPT+C program with bounded variables behaves identically on both, a contradiction.
quote: Counting equivalence forces the same halt stage and output on the two structures, contradicting their opposite query answers.

backbone: A transfinitely built monoid of diagrams and a product forcing give a symmetric submodel with a non-wellorderable set of generic subsets of ω1; quotient analysis yields PP, AC_WO, ¬AC.
quote: We construct a set $A$ of distinct generic subsets of the ground-model $\omega_1$. Symmetry prevents $A$ from being wellordered.

backbone: Reduce to finite specifications; build sort-profile reducibility candidates component by component of the dependency graph, excluding the forbidden configuration by a guarded diagonal argument contradicting weak normalization.
quote: If the interface can be implemented at every strongly connected component, then every legal expression of the PTS is strongly normalizing.

backbone: By Bonk–Kleiner it suffices that combinatorial modulus M(n) is bounded; assuming it is unbounded, record scales produce a limiting function/measure, and both exponential and subexponential record-growth cases lead to contradictions.
quote: The classical criterion reduces the theorem to \[ \sup_n M(n)<\infty. \] Assume this fails. Record indices permit comparison of $M(N-l)$ with $M(N)$, and lead to two growth cases.

backbone: Take periodic St_12(R) over a hierarchically presented graded nil algebra; phases of long words let degree truncations detect all elements, including the central kernel, with homological stability at fixed rank.
quote: Phases of long words in the companion's graded algebra allow finite degree truncations to detect all elements of $\Gamma$, including the central kernel.

backbone: A recursive Hilbert-ball colouring of dyadic partitions turns approximate invariance of a finite set into an approximate fixed point of an explicit positive-displacement map, giving a uniform Følner-defect bound.
quote: The proof turns approximate translation invariance of finite averages of scalar functions on \(F\) into an approximate fixed point of a Lipschitz map on a Hilbert ball.

backbone: Take a RAAG height kernel over an acyclic flag complex with quaternion monodromy (cd 2); a 2-dimensional K(G,1) would force SU(2) presentation rigidity, contradicted by small transport with nontrivial holonomy.
quote: We construct a finitely generated residually finite group of integral cohomological dimension two and geometric dimension three, disproving the Eilenberg--Ganea conjecture.

backbone: Build a finitely presented algebra with simple subalgebra, giving a finitely presented affine group with faithful oligomorphic two-transitive action containing G; twisted Brin–Thompson yields the simple overgroup.
quote: Over \(k=\F_2\), we construct a finitely presented algebra \(B\), a simple subalgebra \(A\subseteq B\) with its own identity, and an injective nonunital map \(\phi:B\to B\) with image in \(A\).

backbone: For nonamenable G, sparse assignments and random sign vectors give block operators with large invariant-kernel energy; a direct-sum triangular cocycle yields a uniformly bounded non-unitarizable representation.
quote: For every discrete nonamenable group \(G\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there are a complex Hilbert space \(\mathcal K\) and a representation \(\pi:G\to\mathrm{GL}(\mathcal K)\) with \(|\pi|\le1+\varepsilon\) that is not similar to a unitary representation.

backbone: Construct a finite Euclidean triangle complex meeting an angular link-excess criterion (torsion-free hyperbolic); rank obstructions over fields put some member of a fixed finite family in the finite residual.
quote: The argument is existential: it proves that one fixed member works for all finite quotients, without identifying which member.

backbone: Construct derived groups of polygon full groups: simple, amenable via random polygonal partitions, Schur multiplier finitely generated via homological stability; a finitely presented central cover then gives the required group.
quote: We construct an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group, giving a positive answer to the finite-presentation existence question for simple amenable groups.
